rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: New-since-pin candidates: chunk 0, line 13 "...the choice is deliberate. It is the simplest store for personal rules there is... And it parks the bigger question..." — both 'it's resolve to `./CLAUDE.local.md`, named at line 5 and again at the start of the same line 13, held within one paragraph. Chunk 4, line 46 "your rules files" (plural) — two distinct rules files are already named earlier in the deck: the personal `./CLAUDE.local.md` (chunk 0/1, repeatedly) and the team `./CLAUDE.md` (named in the compound-and-close-1 prompt fence at chunk 1, "not the team ./CLAUDE.md", and echoed at chunk 0 line 13's "a team's rules and guardrails"), so the plural resolves to that named pair rather than dangling. Unchanged candidates still hold: chunk 2 line 30 "Read Claude's summary" (session-artifact carve-out); chunk 3 line 35 "the compound step added it to your .gitignore" ('it' = CLAUDE.local.md, 'the compound step' = chunk 1's action). No pronoun/demonstrative/noun-phrase fails to resolve.

No sentence in the body (lines 1-49) points at another file by position. `close-the-ticket` is named only in the post-maintainer-cut Arc block (line 111), outside judged scope. Diff added no new cross-file reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0, line 11: "The PR shipped and the ticket is closed." (wording changed by the diff, referent unchanged). Arc block (line 111) confirms this exercise picks up from `close-the-ticket`, which ships the PR and closes the ticket per `getting-going.md` line 123's module flow. Referenced beat exists.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the body; this exercise is a compound/retro loop, not a live-demo beat.

Smallest chunk is chunk 3 (lines 33-36): "If `CLAUDE.local.md` wasn't already ignored, the compound step added it to your `.gitignore`. That is an uncommitted change now; commit it, or drop it." Self-carrying claim (instruction plus decision), not a wait-state bullet. No chunk in the file is content-free. (The prior chunk 5 "What you built", the only chunk close to orphan-shaped, was cut by this diff entirely — nothing to evaluate there now.)

Chunk 0 has no `##` header (H1 only, title slide) but the new lines 13/15 (rules-file location, 'this will bloat') stay on-topic for 'Compound and close the loop'. Chunk 1 'Write your rules file from the session' -> body writes the rules file (lines 19-21). Chunk 2 'Push back where the summary misreads' -> body pushes back (lines 30-31). Chunk 3 'Keep or revert the .gitignore edit' -> body does exactly that (line 35). Chunk 4 'Sweep the session into your rules file one more time' -> second-sweep prompt (lines 39-44) plus the new token-cost aside (line 46) and escape-hatch note (line 48), both about managing the resulting file, not a topic the header contradicts. No header the chunk's own content contradicts.

Checked all sub-items against the full body, with extra attention to the diff's new text (lines 11, 13, 15, 46). Line 11's 'later it will be a test, a doc, a check' is a flat three-noun list, not the banned 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' negation construction and not an anaphora/epistrophe triple (no repeated clause-opening or clause-closing word) — stays inside. Line 13's 'one file, gitignored, read at the top of every session in this repo' is descriptive apposition, not a triplet tic. No self-grading superlative (closest remains line 9's 'every push-back is a hint toward your own rules', a claim about the student's own action, not a rating of the exercise). No number-plus-retraction pattern. No abstraction-noun stacks — new vocabulary stays concrete ('store', 'starter', 'bloat', 'tokens'). No empty-leg verb triplets. None of the six sub-items fire in any chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for repo dialect terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections) in the body (lines 1-49): no hits. 'compound engineering' no longer appears as a bare named term in the body at all (the diff replaced 'the closing step of compound engineering' with the plain-language 'make the next one easier with what this one taught', per the new `compound-definition-plain` claim at line 74) — dialect exposure went down, not up. 'compound' as a verb ('compound the session', 'compound step') is the training's own kit term (`vocabulary.md`), not maintainer-internal shorthand.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 carries 4 bold spans (**Time:**, **What you do:**, **What you build:**, **The point:**) — house exercise-header widget-chrome convention: `grep -rn '^\*\*Time:\*\*' curriculum/exercises/*.md | wc -l` -> 37 files use this identical pattern, unchanged by this diff, and the file's own maintainer block (line 56) attests it stays bold. New body lines 11/13/15/46 add zero new bold. Chunk 1's blockquote bold lead (line 23, 'Long session, long read.') and chunk 4's (line 48, 'The escape hatch is deliberate.') are single callout handles, unchanged, 1 per chunk, within the <=1 non-chrome budget. Body bullet leads (lines 19-21, 30-31, 35, 39-40) are de-bolded, matching the maintainer note's own claim, which was correctly updated by this diff to drop '**What happened:**' from the chrome list now that the section carrying it is gone. No violation.
